6142: /**
6143:  * g_variant_new_from_data:
6144:  * @type: a definite #GVariantType
6145:  * @data: (array length=size) (element-type guint8): the serialized data
6146:  * @size: the size of @data
6147:  * @trusted: %TRUE if @data is definitely in normal form
6148:  * @notify: (scope async): function to call when @data is no longer needed
6149:  * @user_data: data for @notify
6150:  *
6151:  * Creates a new #GVariant instance from serialized data.
6152:  *
6153:  * @type is the type of #GVariant instance that will be constructed.
6154:  * The interpretation of @data depends on knowing the type.
6155:  *
6156:  * @data is not modified by this function and must remain valid with an
6157:  * unchanging value until such a time as @notify is called with
6158:  * @user_data.  If the contents of @data change before that time then
6159:  * the result is undefined.
6160:  *
6161:  * If @data is trusted to be serialized data in normal form then
6162:  * @trusted should be %TRUE.  This applies to serialized data created
6163:  * within this process or read from a trusted location on the disk (such
6164:  * as a file installed in /usr/lib alongside your application).  You
6165:  * should set trusted to %FALSE if @data is read from the network, a
6166:  * file in the user's home directory, etc.
6167:  *
6168:  * If @data was not stored in this machine's native endianness, any multi-byte
6169:  * numeric values in the returned variant will also be in non-native
6170:  * endianness. g_variant_byteswap() can be used to recover the original values.
6171:  *
6172:  * @notify will be called with @user_data when @data is no longer
6173:  * needed.  The exact time of this call is unspecified and might even be
6174:  * before this function returns.
6175:  *
6176:  * Note: @data must be backed by memory that is aligned appropriately for the
6177:  * @type being loaded. Otherwise this function will internally create a copy of
6178:  * the memory (since GLib 2.60) or (in older versions) fail and exit the
6179:  * process.
6180:  *
6181:  * Returns: (transfer none): a new floating #GVariant of type @type
6182:  *
6183:  * Since: 2.24
6184:  **/
6185: GVariant *
6186: g_variant_new_from_data (const GVariantType *type,
6187:                          gconstpointer       data,
6188:                          gsize               size,
6189:                          gboolean            trusted,
6190:                          GDestroyNotify      notify,
6191:                          gpointer            user_data)
6192: {
6193:   GVariant *value;
6194:   GBytes *bytes;
6195: 
6196:   g_return_val_if_fail (g_variant_type_is_definite (type), NULL);
6197:   g_return_val_if_fail (data != NULL || size == 0, NULL);
6198: 
6199:   if (notify)
6200:     bytes = g_bytes_new_with_free_func (data, size, notify, user_data);
6201:   else
6202:     bytes = g_bytes_new_static (data, size);
6203: 
6204:   value = g_variant_new_from_bytes (type, bytes, trusted);
6205:   g_bytes_unref (bytes);
6206: 
6207:   return value;
6208: }
